claims.text: probe's answer is defined by being the ONLY line that does.
claims.why: Comment refers to summary targets being the only ones mentioning rollback; the logic is in _summaries function which picks from _SUMMARY_TARGETS, but the claim about 'only line' is not verifiable from this chunk alone (depends on content of strings).

claims.text: ~40 lines of filler is roughly 800 tokens: long enough that a transport which truncates has something to truncate, and far enough under the Ollama usable input window that the probe itself never provokes the failure it measures.
claims.why: Token count estimate and Ollama window size are not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Both incidents were truncation, in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, so one token cannot catch both
claims.why: Refers to incidents outside this chunk.

claims.text: Ollama HEAD-truncates an over-budget prompt (it eats the system prompt first), so the HEAD token disappears;
claims.why: Behaviour of external system not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: the npm .cmd shim cut a multi-line argv at the first newline, so the TAIL -- including the instruction telling the model what to do -- disappeared, and the model answered 'your message was cut off'.
claims.why: Behaviour of external system not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Requiring BOTH tokens back is what makes a single cheap probe cover both. It also closes the obvious false pass: a model that lost the tail may still echo the head token while complaining about the cut, and that reply is correctly rejected because it cannot contain a tail word it never received.
claims.why: The logic in check_arrival checks for both head token and tail word; if tail is missing, returns False.

claims.text: Strip TRANSPORT artefacts only -- never content. Code fences, surrounding quotes and stray whitespace are things a CLI wrapper adds; removing them keeps the probe measuring instruction-following rather than punishing a lane for its own output framing. Anything the model actually chose to say survives this and is judged.
claims.why: The function strips fences, quotes, and whitespace, and does not remove any other content.

claims.text: It knew the answer and said more anyway. That is the degradation this probe exists for -- a lane that is alive and no longer obedient.
claims.why: The check returns False with 'not_exact' if the wanted string is present but not exact match.

claims.text: Detect a lane that copied the decoy instead of answering. Reported as a QUALITY signal by PROBES: a model anchoring on a prior turn is alive, reachable and useless for reasoning work. Calling that a liveness failure would page someone about a model choice; calling it nothing is how it went unnoticed for a day.
claims.why: The function checks for decoy word in reply and returns 'anchored_on_decoy' if present.

claims.text: The nonce is deliberately NOT in this prompt: the answer is a digit, and a nonce full of digits would give a lazy checker something to trip over.
claims.why: The function does not include nonce in the prompt string.

claims.text: Exactly one of them mentions a rollback. Which one? Answer with just its number.
claims.why: The claim about summaries mentioning rollback depends on content of _SUMMARY_TARGETS, which are defined in this chunk but the actual strings are not shown; the logic in _summaries picks one target from _SUMMARY_TARGETS, so at least one mentions rollback, but 'exactly one' is guaranteed by construction (only one line replaced).

claims.text: A probe is (prompt, checker) and the checker is deterministic Python.
claims.why: ProbeSpec has build and check fields; check functions are deterministic given same nonce and reply.

observations.what: The _filler function references _FILLER_WORDS which is not defined in this chunk; will cause NameError at runtime.
The _anchor_pair function references _ANCHOR_SETS which is not defined in this chunk; will cause NameError at runtime.
The PROBES tuple references SEVERITIES which is not defined in this chunk; will cause NameError at runtime.
The check_arrival function uses re.IGNORECASE on the tail word, which may cause false negatives if the tail word is case-sensitive and the model uses different casing.
The check_comprehension function only checks the first number found in the reply; if the reply contains multiple numbers, it may miss the correct one.
The _summaries function uses rng.sample on _SUMMARY_DECOYS which has only 8 elements; sample(3) is safe, but if _SUMMARY_DECOYS were shorter, it would raise ValueError.
The _anchor_pair function uses rng.sample on _ANCHOR_SETS; if _ANCHOR_SETS is defined elsewhere but has fewer than 2 elements, it will raise ValueError.
The check_anchoring function uses word set from reply; if the correct or decoy word appears as part of another word (e.g., 'back' in 'rollback'), it may cause false positive.
